notes: Sunday: 6-a-side football, expect ~6 km of rapid intervals. Monday was the all-out baseline 5K. Happy to run the rest as needed. Aiming for sub-20 by 10 Dec.
summary: Week 1 of 6. Monday's 22:04 sets your baseline at VDOT 44.4; sub-20 needs 49.9, so you need about +1 VDOT a week for five weeks. That's roughly double a typical rate, so every week has to count. This week absorbs Monday's all-out effort, then puts one sharp session on Thursday at 4:06–4:10/km, already between your interval pace (4:18) and goal pace (4:00). Sunday's football is your second hard day, so Saturday is fully off. Running goes up from ~14 km a week recently to ~25 km this week, the main risk. If calves or shins complain after Thursday, cut Friday to 3 km or skip it.

sessions.title: Baseline 5K
sessions.details: All-out 5K to set the starting point.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.why: An all-out 5K takes 48–72 hours to absorb. Resting today lets Thursday's session be a real quality day.
tips: 10 minutes of easy mobility (calves, hips, hamstrings) is enough.
Get a full night's sleep; it's the best recovery tool you have.

sessions.title: Easy run + strides
sessions.details: 6 km relaxed at 5:25–5:50/km, then 6 × 20 s strides (fast but smooth) with a full walk-back recovery.
sessions.why: Flushes Monday's effort and builds easy volume. The strides keep the legs sharp for Thursday. Cushioned Vomero, since your legs are still recovering.
tips: Easy means conversational. If power climbs above 300 W, slow down.
Do the strides on flat ground and stop at fast-but-relaxed, not a sprint.
Your runs don't record HR yet, so use power and talk-test as your guide.

sessions.title: Intervals: 6 × 800 m
sessions.details: 2 km easy + drills + 4 strides · 6 × 800 m @ 4:06–4:10/km (3:17–3:20 per rep), 400 m easy jog between · 1.5 km cool-down.
sessions.why: Your key session: 800 m reps at a pace between your current interval pace (4:18) and goal pace (4:00) teach your body sub-20 speed in pieces short enough to hold. The Cloudmonster already handled Monday's 5K, so it suits this session and saves the Vaporfly for goal-pace and race days.
tips: Track or a flat, measured loop. Lap every rep so the app can read your splits.
Rep 1 should feel controlled. Run every rep within 2 s of the others. A fast first rep and a fade is the most common mistake.
If you can't hold 4:10 by rep 5, stop at 5. Quality beats completion.
Power target 385–395 W. HR lags on 800s, so pace by power or splits.

sessions.title: Easy aerobic run
sessions.details: 5 km relaxed at 5:30–5:55/km. No strides today.
sessions.why: Easy volume the day after intervals. It builds aerobic base without adding stress before Sunday's football.
tips: Truly easy. Being slower than you think you should be is the point.
If your legs feel heavy from Thursday, make it 3 km or a rest day. Saturday and Sunday matter more.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.why: Sunday's football is a hard, high-intensity session. Arrive fresh so it adds fitness, not fatigue or a tweak.
tips: Hydrate well and eat normal carbs today.
Light calf and hip mobility in the evening.

sessions.title: 6-a-side football (≈6 km of sprints)
sessions.details: Match play: about 6 km of repeated sprints, changes of direction and jogging. This is your second hard session of the week. Do no extra running today.
sessions.why: Repeated sprints are real VO₂max and anaerobic work, so football counts as a quality session. The lateral cuts are the injury risk, not the distance.
tips: Warm up properly: 8–10 min of easy jogging, leg swings, skips and a few short accelerations before kick-off.
Wear football boots or astro trainers, not your running shoes.
Record it on Strava (as football/workout) so next week's plan accounts for the load.
Afterwards: refuel within an hour and stretch calves and hips. Monday will be an easy day.
